items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Uncle Coleman had built many of the houses as he was a Jack of all trades... Uncle Coleman's home

ctx.x: The population was mostly negro, but the general store, the blacksmith shop, and the thrasher machine were owned by white people, and the village doctor for everybody was white. The village was beautiful because some part of it was on a hill and the houses were all built of wood except the Baptist Church, which was built with bricks. Uncle Coleman had built many of the houses as he was a Jack of all trades, and good at all of them. He built the school and his own house which was the largest in the village.

I also remember that my grand-mother Coleman lived in a 4-room log cabin. Any house built of logs was a cabin and this was the only one in Centerville. I never knew if it was Uncle John that built it.

All around Centerville were farms, and some of them belonging to one family which would run as far as the eye could see. The two largest farms were owned by the Fergusons and the Hagens. The Fergusons' land was on the Lexington and Georgetown Road and the Hagen's farm was on the Lexington Road which ran through Centerville. I loved ponies, and there were thousands of them on these two farms.
